subject: Next steps: integration architecture options + tool fallback strategy
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finapp.com>, Anika Bose <anika.bose@finapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + three recommended integration pathways (summary + attachments)

Hi Liam / Anika —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and three pragmatic integration pathways we discussed for embedding Redwood into FinApp's underwriting pipeline. Attached is a one-pager with diagrams (FinApp_integration_options.pdf).

Key constraints you flagged:
- Hard SLO: 90th pct latency < 150ms for individual scoring calls (batching acceptable for async workflows)
- Sensitive data: PII in prompts, requires customer-managed KMS and audit logs
- Reranker/embeddings used for candidate recall with frequent retrain cadence (~weekly)
- Preference to avoid a heavy ops lift on your side for initial PoC

Three recommended options (high-level):
1) Hosted Redwood API + local tool runner (fastest PoC)
   - Redwood hosted models for generation + tools invoked via a small, stateless runner in your VPC (webhook style).
   - Pros: fastest to demo, minimal infra. Cons: needs secure webhook tunnel + token management.
2) Dedicated Instance (reserved capacity) inside your VPC
   - Full inference inside your network, KMS integration, private routing. Use Redwood function-calling + embedded reranker.
   - Pros: meets compliance, predictable latency. Cons: longer setup time, reserved spend.
3) Hybrid: routing layer + model variants
   - Control plane in-hosted; sensitive prompts routed to Dedicated/private model; non-sensitive to hosted to reduce cost. Automatic fallback to smaller quantized model on overload.

Tool/function calling pattern considerations (we discussed):
- Define tool contracts (input/outputs) with strict JSON schema to keep deterministic routing and easy retries.
- Use structured output for classification + tool invocation markers rather than freeform strings.
- Parallelize non-dependent tools (e.g., static enrichment + embeddings lookup) to save wall-clock time; orchestrate dependent calls sequentially.
- Built-in fallback policy: on tool timeout -> retry once with exponential backoff; on tool failure -> mark tool result as stale and continue with degraded path.

Requested next steps (proposal):
- Quick tech workshop (60 min) with your infra and SRE (target next week).
- PoC plan: 2-week sandbox with hosted API + local runner, measure latencies and failure modes.
- Marissa / Rishi to draft tool contracts and a sample schema for candidate scoring.

Action owners:
- Sean: schedule workshop and share calendar invite
- Marissa: draft schema + attach auth snippet (redwood_sdk_auth_snippet.txt)
- Rishi: baseline latency projections + fallback playbook

Attachments: FinApp_integration_options.pdf

Thanks — shout if I missed anything.

—Sean

Hi Liam / Anika —

Quick technical responses so the workshop can be focused: 

1) Embeddings & storage- For a PoC we typically recommend using a managed vector store (e.g., Pinecone, Redis Vector, or your cloud provider's offering) to avoid infra churn. Store metadata pointers to your DB. Weekly rebuilds: incremental update (upsert) pattern keeps throughput low — expect ~5–10k vectors/minute depending on vector dim. We'll size the PoC based on sample corpus.

2) Parallel tools pattern- Pattern we use in production:
   a) Classify whether tools are dependent. If not, fan-out concurrently.
   b) Use a deadline-based approach: set a per-tool soft timeout (e.g., 200ms) and a hard deadline for the aggregate operation (e.g., 350ms) to guarantee SLOs.
   c) If a tool misses deadline, return partial results and add an async reconciliation task (re-score candidate later). This prevents head-of-line blocking while maintaining correctness guarantees.

3) Error handling / observability- Dedicated gives richer audit log options out of the box (audit log sink, KMS integration). For hosted PoC, we instrument at the runner level: log prompt hash, model version, tool call results (status code + latency) to your observability pipeline. We'll share a sample schema.

Tool definition guidance (attached sample snippets):
- Contract first: each tool has name, version, input_schema (JSON Schema), output_schema (JSON Schema), and failure_modes (retryable, non-retryable).
- Structured output: prefer model -> {action: 'call_tool', tool: 'enrichment-v1', args: {}} rather than free text. This reduces downstream parsing fragility.

Auth snippet attached: redwood_sdk_auth_snippet.txt — shows short-lived token rotation + KMS-wrapped secrets for the local runner.

I'll add these items to the workshop agenda and prepare a short demo of the runner's failure/fallback behavior.

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of very specific asks to make the PoC productive: 

- Can you include a minimal auth flow diagram for the hosted runner option showing token issuance, rotation, and what we need to store in KMS?
- For the parallelization approach, can you include a small sequence diagram (fanout -> tool nodes -> aggregator) showing the soft/hard timeout behavior?
- If a tool returns a non-retryable error (business rule violation), should we return a negative signal to the model (so it can attempt alternative logic) or swallow and continue?

We want the PoC to mimic production failure modes, so the above are important. If the workshop can include an SRE from your side that can walk us through the runner's observability hooks, that would be perfect.

Anika
Senior Eng, FinApp

Concrete PoC plan (2 weeks):
Week 0 (setup) — config + access:
- FinApp: create test dataset + vector seed; provide SRE for workshop (owner: Anika)
- Redwood: provision sandbox API keys, provide local runner image and auth snippet (owner: Marissa)

Week 1 — integration + run tests:
- Implement runner webhook, wire embeddings -> managed vector store, implement two tools (enrichment, fraud-check).
- Measure 90th pct latency and error rates. Collect logs. (owner: Jordan / Rishi)

Week 2 — resilience + handoff:
- Add fallback behavior: timeouts, one retry, degraded path. Run chaos test (delayed tool).
- Draft handoff doc and cost estimate for Dedicated if you want to move to private. (owner: Marissa / Sean)

Success criteria for PoC:
- 90th pct latency < 200ms for scoring flow with partial tool fanout
- End-to-end audit log with prompt hash, model version, tool statuses
- Embeddings upsert latency < target for weekly rebuilds

Follow-ups I will send immediately after the workshop:
- Integration playbook (integration-fallback-playbook.md)
- Sample JSON schema for tool contracts
- Demo recording + raw metrics from the sandbox run

If that looks good I'll coordinate with Procurement on a short-term hosted credit arrangement to run the PoC without Reserved spend.

Thanks all — see you Tue.

—Sean
